text: HCM City, Singapore push investment ties into tech, sustainable growth

HCM CITY - Singapore and Việt Nam have built a strong partnership founded on mutual trust, complementary strengths and shared aspirations, according to Pang Te Cheng, Consul General of Singapore in HCM City

"I am confident that HCM City, with its entrepreneurial energy and ambitious development plans, will play a leading role in the next chapter of Singapore-Việt Nam economic relations", he said at the HCM City-Singapore Investment Promotion Conference.
The event was organised by the Investment and Trade Promotion Centre of HCM City (ITPC) to engage Singaporean businesses and present the city's policies and priority projects.

Pang highlighted that despite global economic uncertainties and trade tensions, Việt Nam has demonstrated remarkable resilience in the first nine months of 2026, and HCM City has been at the forefront of this growth.
Pang also mentioned that Việt Nam's mid-term outlook remains promising, supported by its competitive manufacturing base, expanding domestic market and ambitious infrastructure development.

He said the bilateral partnership is entering a new phase after Singapore and Việt Nam elevated ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in March 2025 and the Việt Nam-Singapore Joint Statement on Strategic Technology Connectivity issued in August this year, reflecting their shared ambition to become leading strategic technology partners in Southeast Asia.
"These agreements provide a strong framework to expand our cooperation beyond traditional trade and investment into innovation, emerging technologies, and sustainable development," he said.

He emphasised four promising areas for deeper Singapore-HCM City cooperation, which are digital infrastructure and artificial intelligence, green energy and sustainability, innovation and talent and finance and logistics.
"These opportunities extend beyond capital investment.
The next phase of our partnership should bring together capital, technology, expertise and talent to create higher value and more sustainable economic activities.

Nguyễn Lộc Hà, Standing Vice Chairman of the HCM City People's Committee, said that as of September 2026, Singapore ranked as the largest source of registered foreign investment in the city, with 2,815 active projects and total registered capital exceeding US$25.28 billion.

He also stressed that this year marks 30 years of development for the Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Park (VSIP) and said the city has agreed in principle for VSIP to study and implement new projects in Vũng Tàu Ward.

In addition, the city leader welcomed Singaporean businesses to expand their investments and deepen cooperation with Vietnamese businesses in technology, services and supply chains to build long-term, effective business partnerships.

Phạm Quang Nhật, director of ITPC, outlined priority areas for cooperation that align the city's strengths with the needs of Singaporean investors, including encouraging Singaporean financial institutions to join the Vietnam International Financial Centre in HCM City.
The city wants to further connect local firms with Singaporean partners in semiconductor research and training, electronic components, microchips and biotechnology.
Currently, Singapore is currently the largest source of foreign direct investment at the Saigon Hi-Tech Park, with 14 projects estimated at $4.96 billion.
It also called for collaboration to develop logistics and port infrastructure, focusing on the Long Sơn General Port project with an estimated investment of VNĐ12 trillion.
For industrial parks, HCM City seeks Singaporean partners for smart, eco-friendly infrastructure and deeper cooperation with existing firms on energy efficiency, resource reuse and emissions cuts.
In addition, the city aims to attract Singaporean capital and expertise in service development, governance and project operations for free trade, commercial-service and urban infrastructure projects.

Key developments include the Cái Mép Hạ Free Trade Zone as well as key urban and commercial-service developments such as the Thủ Thiêm - Long Thành railway line, the Tân An Hội Commercial Centre, the Tha La Peninsula Eco-Tourism and Resort Complex and Saigon Safari Park. - VNS
